messages:
emily (support): Heads-up — AcmeCorp (acct: 9876543210) escalated: their AWS Marketplace invoice INV-2026-0456 shows 1,250,000 token units billed but our Redwood dashboard reports 125,000 tokens for the same period. Customer is very concerned about a 10x delta. Invoice PDF attached by customer. Please triage.
emily (support): Key customer points: invoice period 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28, SKU 'redwood-usage.tokens.aws', line item quantity=1250000, unit=Token, price looks reasonable but quantity mismatch.
ben (billing-eng): thanks emily. can you paste the raw marketplace line items (csv/json) they sent or the invoice extract? also confirm the marketplace account id and the marketplace entitlement mapping we have in datastore.
emily (support): pasted the customer's line item snippet here: ```SKU,Description,Quantity,Unit,Amount
redwood-usage.tokens.aws,Redwood inference tokens,1250000,Token,1250.00```
emily (support): AWS acct id they used to buy = 9876543210. Our internal mapping for that external acct -> Redwood tenant_id = tenant_acme_01.
ben (billing-eng): initial hypothesis: either ingestion applied a multiplier (e.g. per-100-token vs per-token unit conversion) or we accidentally stored 'quantity' as units-of-100. i'll run a quick query.
ben (billing-eng): Query I ran to compare totals (summarized):
```
SELECT invoice_id, SUM(tokens) as dashboard_tokens FROM usage_events
WHERE tenant_id='tenant_acme_01' AND invoice_period='2026-02' GROUP BY invoice_id;
-- result: dashboard_tokens = 125000
```
ben (billing-eng): On the marketplace ingestion side I pulled the processed line_items table and got quantity=1250000. So somewhere in processing there's a factor of 10. :thinking_face:
carla (sre): i checked the ingestion logs for the AWS marketplace S3 batch processed 2026-03-01T03:12Z. The transform step showed this env var: MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_UNIT_MULTIPLIER=10 in the container that ran the job. looks like a legacy var introduced in 2024 and should be 1. logs:```
[2026-03-01T03:12:02Z] INFO ingest.start file=s3://marketplace/9876543210/invoice-2026-02.json
[2026-03-01T03:12:05Z] INFO transform.apply multiplier=10 -> applied to field 'quantity'
[2026-03-01T03:12:06Z] INFO write.line_item sku=redwood-usage.tokens.aws quantity=1250000
```
carla (sre): looks like the ingestion job multiplied the raw AWS quantity by 10 before writing line items to our marketplace_line_items table.
ben (billing-eng): confirmed. the raw AWS payload from their CSV showed 125000 tokens. ingestion multiplied by 10 and produced 1,250,000. that explains the invoice line item count. this means our dashboard query used the raw usage_events feed (125k) but the marketplace ingestion table (used for billing bridge) has the inflated count.
dan (product): are we sure the raw AWS file is 125k not 125k * 10? can carla attach the original S3 object or the customer's CSV to be certain?
carla (sre): attached S3 object contents: ```{"lineItems": [{"sku": "redwood-usage.tokens.aws", "quantity": 125000, "unit": "Token"}], "accountId": "9876543210"}```
ben (billing-eng): good. action items: 1) revert MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_UNIT_MULTIPLIER to 1 in ingestion config (prod & replay), 2) re-run the ingestion job for 2026-02 for that account and regenerate marketplace_line_items, 3) compute delta and propose customer credit or invoice correction, 4) open AWS Marketplace support case if they already invoiced and can't retract.
emily (support): customer is expecting a quick resolution and wants a timeline. Can we get an ETA for re-run and credits?
carla (sre): i'll remove the env var from the deploy config by EOD (today) and kick off a replay job for the affected S3 prefix. replay estimate: ~45m for single-account reprocess. i'll post results and new line_item totals.
ben (billing-eng): once carla posts the corrected quantity i'll calculate the billing delta and recommend credit amount. if invoice already charged, we will create a one-off credit in the billing system and coordinate with finance to notify Acme.
dan (product): we should also audit other tenant accounts ingested during that deploy window (2026-03-01T03:00Z to 03:30Z). if multiplier was on, multiple customers might be affected. please run a quick scan of unique account ids written with multiplier applied.
carla (sre): good call. scanning now -> found 6 account ids with inflated quantities in that run: 9876543210, 1112223334, 2223334445, 3334445556, 4445556667, 5556667778. i'll add them to the replay queue and owner list.
emily (support): documenting for customer: "we discovered an ingestion configuration bug that multiplied marketplace token counts by 10 for a small set of accounts processed on 2026-03-01. We're replaying the ingestion and will issue credits for any confirmed overcharges. ETA for AcmeCorp correction: ~1 hour." :white_check_mark:
ben (billing-eng): after replay -> i ran reconciliation and computed invoice delta for AcmeCorp: billed_tokens=1250000 corrected_tokens=125000 billing_delta_tokens=1125000. credit_amount = prorated_price_per_token * 1125000. i'll prepare the credit memo and include line-item reconciliation CSV.
carla (sre): replay finished: corrected marketplace_line_items now show quantity=125000 for INV-2026-0456. attached reconciliation CSV.
ben (billing-eng): confirmed reconciliation matches our dashboard. creating Billing Credit BC-2026-089 for AcmeCorp and notifying finance + emily.
emily (support): emailed AcmeCorp with explanation and credit promise. customer replied: "Thanks for the quick fix. Please confirm the credit appears on our March statement." i'll keep them posted.
dan (product): we should add a unit test to the ingest pipeline to assert MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_UNIT_MULTIPLIER defaults to 1 and fail CI if set to >1 for token skus. filing a ticket in infra backlog.
carla (sre): opened infra ticket INFRA-2026-112. also added monitoring alert for unexpected multiplier env values.
ben (billing-eng): closing loop: BC-2026-089 created, finance confirmed credit will be applied to next statement. i'll attach the credit memo to this thread. :white_check_mark:
emily (support): great work team. closing this thread after customer confirms credit on their next statement. :thumbsup:
